description: Backend-developer handover manifest. Machine-readable index of front-end elements that are mock / visual-only / in-memory and need real backend implementation. Front-end-only repo (vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, no backend). See HANDOVER.md for the human-readable version and the TODO(backend:<Surface>) in-code marker convention.

categories.visual-only: Rendered but no behaviour wired at all.
categories.fe-wired: Works client-side; no backend required (may be fine as-is).
categories.needs-backend: Requires real data, API, auth, persistence, or AI service.

Login.note: CC Control Centre login screen. Standalone visual mock — the form renders but no authentication, session, or validation is wired.

items.current: Form submits to '#'; no auth, no validation.
items.needs: POST /auth/login { email, password, remember } → establish session and redirect to the Control Centre; surface invalid-credential / field errors on the inputs (Input has an error state).

items.element: .checkbox ("Remember me", name="remember")
items.current: Toggles visually only.
items.needs: Bind to session lifetime on login — persistent cookie when checked, session cookie otherwise.

items.element: .cc-login__link ("Forgot password?", href="#")
items.current: Links to '#'.
items.needs: Route to /auth/forgot (password-reset flow).

items.element: .cc-login__link ("Register Now", href="#")
items.current: Links to '#'.
items.needs: Route to /auth/register (sign-up flow).

ControlHub.note: CC filterable directory screen. Reuses the ControlScreen app-shell (see the ControlScreen surface for all shell-level backend items — sidebar nav, auth, notifications, AI assistant, favourites, etc.). The items below are specific to ControlHub's own page content; everything else is inherited from the reused shell.

items.element: .cc-directory__filter .input__control (placeholder 'Filter...')
items.current: Filter field renders (search icon + clear button) but no filtering logic is wired — typing does nothing; the clear button is the component default only.
items.needs: Client-side filtering is sufficient (no backend): debounced text match over ActionCard titles across all sections, hiding cards (and empty section headings) that don't match; clear button resets. Promote to fe-wired once implemented.

items.element: .action-card--chevron (href="#") + .action-card--button (whole-card nav, pointer cursor) with a separate .btn ("+ add")
items.current: Both card variants are meant to navigate the whole card to the area's screen. Chevron cards link to '#'; Button cards show a pointer cursor but card-level navigation isn't wired; the 'add' buttons are inert.
items.needs: Real navigation targets per area for BOTH variants (whole card → the corresponding report/analysis screen — implement the Button card as a stretched-link so the '+ add' button stays a separate action above it) and an add-to-favourites/dashboard action for the 'add' button (POST, then reflect added state). Card title + section taxonomy comes from the same content source as the sidebar nav.

ControlScreen.note: CC home/landing dashboard. Front-end complete; all data is hardcoded and most actions are mock. Composes many CC patterns — see docs/component-registry.md for per-component status.

items.element: saveFav() / removeFav() + .cc-control__fav-list (desktop + mobile)
items.current: Saving/removing a favourite only mutates the DOM in memory; lost on reload. Mirrored across both list copies.
items.needs: Favourites CRUD API: GET (load on init), POST (save {name, context, timestamp}), DELETE. Replace in-memory DOM mutation with API-backed state.

items.element: initSubmenuPins() in patterns/SidebarMenu/sidebar-menu.js + .cc-menu__submenu-item--pinned
items.current: Pinning a nav sub-item floats it to the top (order:-1) and fills the pin icon, but state is in-memory only — held on the DOM, scoped to one menu tree (not synced desktop↔mobile) and lost on reload.
items.needs: Persist pinned sub-items via a user-prefs API: GET pinned ids on init (apply --pinned on render), POST on pin, DELETE on unpin. Key by user + menu item id; share state across the desktop and mobile menu trees.

items.needs: Per-panel search/filter API (debounced query → results), populate the lists from the response.

items.element: Static submenu <li> links in the SidebarMenu panels (CRM/Content/Marketing/etc.)

items.needs: Menu/structure API to populate items; permission-based visibility; real navigation/routing on click.

items.element: Zone Selector dropdown (.sel, wired by Select.js for open/close only)

items.needs: Load available zones; persist selection to session; reload dashboard data for the chosen zone.

items.element: 2 Chart.js charts (Page Views, Users) + time-range buttons + report links
items.current: Hardcoded data arrays + static labels; range buttons and report links are visual only.
items.needs: Analytics API for series data; time-range query (7d/30d/etc.) updating the chart; real routes for Clicks/Revenue reports.

items.needs: Users API with server-side paginate/sort/search; live 'online' status (poll or WebSocket); touch/login metadata from auth.

AudioPlayer.note: Article audio player component (3 types). Playback is simulated by a JS timer so the scrubber/waveform/time read true in the demo; no real audio is bundled.

EventBuilder.note: AI-driven event builder prototype: brief -> generated draft -> guided gap-filling -> block library -> in-context editing -> all-fields form -> published page. Front end only. The entire event model lives in the DOM and is lost on reload (bar the brief, which uses sessionStorage). Blocks map 1:1 to existing Advanced Event fields; no new event capability is implied.

items.element: 01-brief.html `.msg-input__textarea[data-eb-brief]` + send button
items.current: Brief is typed and stashed in sessionStorage under `eb:brief`; the send button just navigates to 02.
items.needs: POST /api/event-builder/generate { brief, sectionId } -> full event model: chosen blocks + order, page shape (tabbed|scroll), first-pass field values, and a per-field confidence so the gap-fill list on 04 can be derived rather than hardcoded.

items.element: 02-generating.html `.eb-gen__list` progress items
items.current: Hardcoded checklist with static done/working/pending states; the spinner is decorative.
items.needs: Stream generation events (block decided / copy written / field inferred) over SSE or websocket from the generate call, so progress reflects real work.

items.element: 03-draft.html `[data-eb-proposal]` cards + the in-canvas `.eb-block--proposed` action bar
items.current: Three static proposals. Accept/Reject rewrite the DOM (accept clears the dashed state, reject removes the block and its rail row); nothing persists.
items.needs: Return proposals as a diff against the current event model, each with a target block, a payload and a provenance reference (e.g. 'from your 2026 page'). Accept applies the patch server-side and returns the new model; reject records the dismissal so it is not re-proposed.

items.element: `.eb-promptbar__input[data-eb-prompt]` on 03, 04, 06 and 07
items.current: Free-text prompt bar; Refine buttons pre-fill it. Submitting does nothing.
items.needs: POST /api/event-builder/refine { eventId, prompt, selectedBlockId? } -> a proposal diff rendered through the same accept/reject path as eb-proposals.

items.element: 04-gapfill.html `.eb-answer` judge checkbox list; 'Select all 16' / 'Add someone new'
items.current: Five hardcoded contacts; checkboxes toggle but the count in the button is static and nothing is written.
items.needs: GET /api/crm/contacts?role=judge&event=<prevEventId> for the candidate list, then write chosen contact ids to the event's speakers field (the same field the Advanced Event screen uses). Also needs contact-create for 'Add someone new'.

items.element: 05-blocks.html `[data-eb-add]` library cards; rail `[data-eb-move]` / `[data-eb-remove]`
items.current: Adding appends a rail row and flips the card to 'In use'; reorder swaps DOM siblings and re-appends canvas blocks; remove deletes both. All in-memory.
items.needs: Block membership + order persisted on the event, and the section/article scaffolding each block implies created server-side (this is the work the 'Created for you' notices describe). Locked 'Coming later' cards are deliberately inert.

items.element: `[data-eb-shape]` in the inspector on 03 and 06
items.current: Toggling swaps the tab strip for the sticky anchor nav and shows/hides `[data-eb-panel]` groups. Works fully client-side.
items.needs: Persist the chosen shape on the event and have the public template honour it. The rendering logic itself is front-end and can ship as-is.

items.element: 06-inline-edit.html `.eb-editable[contenteditable]` regions + `.eb-formatbar`
items.current: Text is editable in the browser and the format bar is decorative. Edits are never saved and the 'Rewrite with AI' / 'Shorten' buttons do nothing.
items.needs: PATCH the corresponding event field per edited region (each editable needs a field binding), plus an AI rewrite endpoint for the two assistive format-bar actions. Undo needs a revision history.

items.element: `.drag-drop[data-drag-drop]` on 06 (hero background) and 07 (main / alternative image)
items.current: Drop zones render; no file is read or stored.
items.needs: POST /api/media/upload -> media-library reference stored on the block/field. Should also allow picking an existing media-library item rather than only uploading.

items.element: 07-advanced.html `#f-cat` / `#f-table` (catalogue items)
items.current: Plain text inputs containing a human-readable item name and price.
items.needs: GET /api/catalogue/items with a picker bound to an item id (not a string), so the event's Buy Now / Book a table buttons resolve to real catalogue items and prices.

items.element: 07-advanced.html `.eb-from` / `.eb-from--canvas` badges and the 'inconsistency' warning
items.current: Static badges marking which fields the assistant wrote vs which were edited on the page; the SEO-title mismatch and its 'Fix it' button are hardcoded.
items.needs: Per-field provenance (who/what last wrote it: assistant, canvas edit, or form) stored with the event, plus a consistency check across related fields (title vs SEO title vs teaser) to generate these warnings.

items.element: `.eb-map` on 03 and 08
items.current: Styled placeholder reading 'Map generated from the address'.
items.needs: Server-side geocode of the venue address returning map tiles or a static map image — the point being a structured address field instead of pasted embed code in the WYSIWYG.

items.element: 'Publish' / 'Save & publish' in the top bar; the 08 confirmation toast
items.current: Navigates to 08-published.html and shows a success toast unconditionally.
items.needs: Persist the event, run the publication rules (go-live date, access clearance, live flag) and return the public URL. The toast should reflect the real result, including validation failures.

items.element: 01-brief.html 'Clone last year's event' action card
items.current: Inert button.
items.needs: GET /api/events?clonable=1 for the picker, then a server-side deep copy of the event model plus its section scaffolding into a new draft.

SeatingPlanner.file: src/cc/patterns/EventPicker/ (screen 1, built) + src/prototypes/SeatingPlanner/ (screen 2 workspace shell, prototype)
SeatingPlanner.note: Control > CRM > Seating Planner. Screen 1 (event picker, TASK-342608) shipped as the EventPicker pattern. Screen 2 is the workspace shell — TASK-344753 — covering the event bar, seating plans row, toolbar, tables grid, seat panel and unassigned tray. That task is the shell + wiring only: each control's detail lives in its own sub-task and is marked up with [data-sp-action] + [data-sp-task], routed through one registry. A sub-task goes live by calling SeatingPlannerWorkspace.on('<action>', fn) — no refactor needed. Reads/writes SeatingPlan, Table and TableSeat (data model on the parent task); no new fields.

items.element: EventPicker rows + predictive search (event-picker.js)
items.current: Rows are mock DOM; search filters already-loaded rows in the browser.
items.needs: GET /crm/events?status=live&sort=-startDate for the list; debounced GET /crm/events?q=<term> for search.

items.element: Pinned "Last used" row; the prototype keeps it in localStorage
items.current: Per-user last-used event is client-side only; the pattern deliberately leaves persistence to the host.
items.needs: Per-user preference read on module open and written on select. Named in the brief as a remaining item.

items.element: workspace-no-event.html — the event-gated entry state
items.current: Static: picker over an empty workspace.
items.needs: Opening the module with no event chosen must show the picker and render nothing else until one is selected (Behaviour section of TASK-344753).

items.element: .sp-plan chips — name, table count, seated/capacity, fill bar
items.current: Two mock plans; chip selection swaps the visible tables client-side.
items.needs: GET the event's SeatingPlan rows with aggregate table/seat counts. Selecting a plan loads its Tables.

items.element: .sp-table cards — name, tier, sponsor, fill pill, seat dots
items.current: 36 mock cards (30 Main Ballroom + 6 Overflow). Fill pill and dots recompute client-side after an unseat.
items.needs: GET Tables for the selected plan with per-seat occupancy so the dots and fill pill derive from real TableSeat rows.

items.element: .sp-panel seat list — occupant, role tag, reorder, remove
items.current: Seats derived from mock dot data; reorder and remove work in the DOM and are lost on reload.
items.needs: Read/write TableSeat. Seat order is meaningful ("who sits next to whom") so reorder must persist an explicit index, not a sort. Remove clears the seat and returns the person to Unassigned.

items.element: Unassigned pool (TASK-351550) — now the DS pattern `src/patterns/Unassigned/` (built 2026-08-25 from Figma `3478:111942`), superseding the prototype's `tray-*.html` + `SeatingPlannerTray.js`
items.current: **DS pattern now exists** and is the authority for the markup: a 320px rail with a count pill, a hint line, a label-less search field (Input) and either an empty state or a list of AttendeeCards with both booleans off. It is presentational — the tray contents, the count, the search filtering and the drag are all unwired, and the rows are the drag SOURCES the seat rows receive. DERIVED, not a list: the event's people minus everyone seated, recomputed on every change. Role tag + name + company per row, live count badge, predictive search over name AND company, and an empty state for a fully-seated event. Because it derives, the four return paths (unseat, delete table, delete plan, reduce capacity) now put people back BY NAME with no pushing — they used to insert a row labelled by origin ("Table 12 · seat 4") because the occupant's real name was not available. Manually-added guests (342309) survive being unseated because the module remembers anyone it has seen seated who is not on the roster.
items.needs: The list is a QUERY, not a stored collection: the event's attendees and linked CRM contacts LEFT JOIN TableSeat, keeping the unseated, plus guests already stored on a TableSeat. No new stored fields. Recompute server-side after every seating change rather than caching client-side, or two editors will disagree about who is free. Owner confirmed: TASK-351550.

items.element: [data-sp-freeseats] toggle
items.current: Filters the grid to tables holding at least one empty seat. Fully working.
items.needs: Nothing server-side while the plan's tables are already loaded. Revisit only if table lists are paginated.

items.element: Every [data-sp-action] control: copy-plans 344756, add-table 344757, room-layout 344760, export 344761, table-edit 342307, table-delete 344758, assign-seat 342309
items.current: EVERY [data-sp-action] control is now built — nothing is left announcing an unbuilt task. The registry has two kinds of extension point: click actions, and 'notify' for a sub-task that owns a derived view (351550).
items.needs: Nothing further front-end. Keep the registry when wiring the backend: it is where each control's handler already lives.

items.element: Drag to seat (TASK-344759) — drag-*.html + SeatingPlannerDrag.js
items.current: All four placements from the brief are live: pool → empty seat, pool → table card (first free seat, or refused with "Table full"), seat → seat (move, or swap when the target is occupied), seat → pool (unseat). Plus seat → another table card, which the brief omits but the interaction implies. Drag shows the source dimmed, legal targets in success tone, a "Swap" label on an occupied seat and the refusal reason on a full table. THE SAME FOUR PLACEMENTS RUN BY TAP AND BY KEYBOARD: pick a person, a bar names who is in the air, then choose a seat, a table or the pool; Esc cancels. Nothing re-implements seating — it moves people between card dots and the occupant list and hands off to the shell, so the pool re-derives itself (351550).
items.needs: Each placement is a TableSeat write — occupant plus seat order. A SWAP is two rows changing in ONE transaction, or the pair can end up in the same seat; a move between tables changes the parent Table too, so it must not be modelled as delete-then-insert. Re-read the plan after a placement rather than trusting the client, since two editors can aim at the same seat.

items.element: Table tier — .sp-table--tier-* left edge + .sp-table__tier label
items.current: RESOLVED BY TASK-342308. Colours no longer come from the design system at all: every card takes its left edge from --sp-tier-colour, painted at runtime from the TableType lookup, so the DS needs no metallic Gold/Silver/Bronze tokens. Seeded Standard #8fa0b5, Gold #c9a227, Silver #b8bfc7, Bronze #b07d48, VIP #9b51e0, Head table #3b6fe0, Sponsor #c0392b. The tier LABEL still always renders, so tier is never colour-only. Premium (used in the earlier build) is not in the brief's set and stays migrated to Gold.
items.needs: Store the colour per TableType row (see seating-table-types). Two of the three original questions survive: a card can still carry three colour systems at once (tier edge, 6 role dot colours, 3 fill states), and VIP/Sponsor are BOTH tier values and role values — Sponsor is also a separate field on the table form, so Type=Sponsor with an empty Sponsor field remains undefined. The metallic-token question is closed.

items.element: New plan popup — src/prototypes/SeatingPlanner/newplan-*.html + SeatingPlannerNewPlan.js
items.current: Modal validates the two required fields and the 6–12 seats bound, then creates the plan chip and generates its table cards entirely in the DOM. Lost on reload. Registers itself on the shell via SeatingPlannerWorkspace.on('new-plan', …) — the shell was not modified.
items.needs: POST a SeatingPlan with { name (required), room, tables (required), seatsPerTable (default 10, bounded 6–12), tableShape (Round|Square) } and an FK to the selected Event; generate Table + TableSeat rows server-side; return the created plan so the plans row and grid re-read rather than being built client-side. Server must re-validate — the client bound is a convenience, not a guarantee.

items.element: Table shape (Round / Square) — set at generation time in the New plan popup
items.current: Captured on the plan and echoed in the confirmation toast, but nothing renders shape: the tables grid shows no shape indicator, and TASK-344753's table cards have no shape affordance.
items.needs: Decide whether shape is display-only metadata or should render on the table card / in the Room layout view (TASK-344760). Raised by this build — the shell predates the field.

items.element: Edit plan popup — src/prototypes/SeatingPlanner/editplan-*.html + SeatingPlannerEditPlan.js
items.current: Opens from a chip's ✎ pre-filled from THAT chip (the shell passes the clicked control through as ctx.trigger). Saving renames the chip, updates its room, rebuilds the label the toolbar reads, and refreshes the action buttons' aria-labels. DOM-only, lost on reload.
items.needs: PATCH the SeatingPlan record with { name (required), room }. Renaming must NOT touch the plan's Tables or TableSeats — verified in the prototype: a rename leaves all 30 tables and the open seat panel intact. Re-read the plans row after saving rather than patching the DOM.

items.element: Delete plan confirmation — deleteplan-confirm.html + SeatingPlannerDeletePlan.js
items.current: alertdialog on a chip's ✕, opened from the clicked chip. Copy is data-driven — table and seated counts are read off the DOM, and the people clause is dropped when nobody is seated. Confirming removes the chip and its table cards, injects every returned occupant into the Unassigned tray, and if the deleted plan was open, selects the next remaining plan (or folds the workspace away and restores the "No plans yet" hint when none are left). Esc cancels. DOM-only.
items.needs: Delete the SeatingPlan plus its Table and TableSeat rows in ONE transaction and return the occupants to the event pool. A partial failure must not leave people unassigned from a plan that still exists. Re-read the plans row and the Unassigned pool after deleting rather than patching the DOM. The counts in the dialog must come from the server, not the client, so a stale page can't understate what is about to be destroyed.

items.element: Copy plans to event — copyplans-*.html + SeatingPlannerCopyPlans.js
items.current: Destination list reuses screen 1's Event Picker rows (.sp-event) and predictive search; the current event is excluded so a plan can't be copied onto itself. Intro copy is data-driven (plan count + source event name read off the page). Selecting a destination bumps that row's plan count and toasts what was copied. DOM-only.
items.needs: Insert cloned SeatingPlan + Table rows under the target Event with TableSeat occupants left EMPTY — tables, capacities, types and sponsors carried, attendees not. Clone in ONE transaction so a failure can't leave half a layout. Destination list is GET /crm/events excluding the current event, with a debounced ?q= search.

items.element: Destination rows showing an existing plan count (e.g. "1 plan")
items.current: Copy is INSERT, not replace: copying 2 plans into an event that already has 1 leaves it with 3. The prototype makes this visible by showing each destination's current plan count and incrementing it, but nothing warns before the fact.
items.needs: Confirm the intended semantics. If append is right, consider naming clones to avoid two plans called "Main Ballroom" in one event. If replace is ever wanted it needs its own confirmation, since it would destroy existing seating. Raised by this build — the brief says "insert" but doesn't cover the collision case.

items.element: Add table toolbar button (TASK-344757) — SeatingPlannerAddTable.js
items.current: No popup. Appends a card with the next table number, the plan's default seat count (data-sp-plan-seats, set when the plan was created), every seat empty; recomputes the plan chip and toolbar count, and opens the new table so its empty seat list is on screen.
items.needs: Insert a Table plus its empty TableSeat rows under the plan. Assign the table number and sort order SERVER-SIDE — computing either on the client races other editors. Note the number must be max(existing)+1, not count+1: after deleting Table 3 of 5, count+1 would mint a second Table 5. Seat count comes from the PLAN default, not from the last table, since individual tables can have been changed.

items.element: Plan chip summary "N tables · X/Y seated · Z free" + its fill bar
items.current: BUG FOUND AND FIXED during TASK-344757: the chip was written once and never recomputed, so the summary went stale the moment anyone was unseated — the plan summary silently lied. syncPlanChip() now recomputes it from the plan's tables and is called on unseat and on add-table; it is published on the shell API for later sub-tasks that add or remove tables.
items.needs: Nothing server-side while a plan's tables are all loaded — the recompute is client-side. Any sub-task that changes table or seat counts must call SeatingPlannerWorkspace.syncPlanChip(planKey), or derive the summary from the server response.

items.element: Table form, New / Edit (TASK-342307) — tableform-*.html + SeatingPlannerTableForm.js
items.current: Opens pre-filled from a table's edit action. Name (required), tier (the 7 named values), sponsor via account lookup with predictive search, host, capacity, shape. Saving rewrites the card's name, tier class + label, sponsor line, dots, count and fill pill, then resyncs the plan chip. DOM-only.
items.needs: Table row with FKs — Type → Table Type lookup, Sponsor → Account — plus a sort order. Accounts list is GET /crm/accounts?q=. Capacity changes must add/remove TableSeat rows and unassign the surplus in the SAME transaction.

items.element: Seats (capacity) field + its data-driven note
items.current: The note states current occupancy and escalates to a warning naming exactly how many people will be displaced before you save. On save the surplus is taken from the HIGHEST-numbered seats and returned to Unassigned; increasing capacity appends empty seats. Verified 10→7 returned 3, and 7→12 added 5 empty.
items.needs: Server must decide and record WHICH occupants are displaced. Taking the last seats is the only sensible automatic rule, but seat order is meaningful here ("who sits next to whom"), so confirm with the spec team whether the user should choose instead of the system picking. Unassign in the same transaction as the seat removal.

items.element: "New table" mode of the table form (tableform-new.html)
items.current: The form supports a New mode and it is captured, but NOTHING opens it: TASK-344757's Add table button creates a table instantly from the plan defaults, with no form.
items.needs: Resolve the overlap between the two briefs. 344757 says Add table adds straight away; 342307 is titled "New / Edit Table form". Either Add table should open this form pre-filled with the defaults, or the New mode is dead and should be dropped. Raised by this build.

items.element: Delete table confirmation (TASK-344758) — deleteplan style, deletetable-confirm.html + SeatingPlannerDeleteTable.js
items.current: alertdialog on a card's ✕, opened from the clicked card. Copy is data-driven (table name + seated count); with nobody seated it says so rather than inventing a consequence. Confirming returns each occupant to Unassigned, removes the card, resyncs the plan chip, and — if the deleted table was the open one — moves the seat panel to the next remaining table, or clears it when the plan has no tables left. Esc cancels. DOM-only.
items.needs: Delete the Table and its TableSeat rows and return occupants to the event pool in ONE transaction. Table numbers are NOT resequenced after a delete: Add table takes max(existing)+1, so gaps are expected and harmless — resequencing would renumber tables under guests who have already been told their table number.

items.element: Table names / numbers across plans
items.current: Table names are unique only WITHIN a plan — Main Ballroom and Overflow Room B both have a "Table 1". Every lookup in the prototype scopes by plan (data-sp-belongs); a selector that doesn't will silently hit the wrong plan's table, which is exactly what happened in one of this build's test assertions.
items.needs: Scope every table query by SeatingPlan, and never treat a table name or number as an event-wide identifier. Worth confirming whether names should be unique per plan at the database level.

items.element: Table types lookup (TASK-342308) — tabletypes-*.html + SeatingPlannerTableTypes.js
items.current: Modal listing the tier set with a colour swatch, an editable label, up/down reorder and Remove per row, plus an add row at the foot. The rows ARE the model: row index is sortOrder. Opened from the toolbar's tier-colours control. Editing a colour repaints every table on that tier live; renaming a tier migrates its tables so identity survives; removing a tier drops its tables back to Standard and says how many moved. Standard cannot be removed — it shows "default" instead of a dead control. Duplicate labels are rejected with a toast. The Table form's tier dropdown is rebuilt from the same list. DOM-only — nothing persists across a reload.
items.needs: A TableType lookup table (label, colour, sortOrder) with Table.Type as an FK to it. Because it is an FK, a delete must either repoint dependent Tables at Standard or be blocked — never left dangling — and a rename must be invisible to the Tables. Enforce label uniqueness server-side and protect the Standard/fallback row from deletion. The seed values above are the brief's list; the colours are a first pass and are the client's to change.

items.element: The colour picker in the Table types lookup
items.current: A free <input type="color">. Client-chosen, so the value is data, not a token — which means nothing stops it colliding with something already meaningful on the same card. The seeded Head table #3b6fe0 already sits very close to the brand blue used for the SELECTED table, and the six role dot hues are in the same space. There is no contrast check against the card background and no mono-print fallback; the tier text label always rendering is the only guarantee that tier survives a bad colour choice.
items.needs: Decide how much to constrain the picker: a curated swatch set is the safest answer, or keep it free and add a contrast check plus a warning when a pick lands near the selection blue or a role colour. Either way keep the tier label visible — colour must never be the only carrier. Raised by this build.

items.element: Sort Order in the Table types lookup
items.current: The brief asks for a Sort Order field; the reference image shows an ordered list with no number. Implemented as row order with up/down controls — the same affordance the seat list uses — and read back as a 0-based sortOrder. The number is the data, the list is the interface.
items.needs: Confirm the list is acceptable in place of a literal number field. If numbers must be editable directly (e.g. to interleave a new tier without dragging), the field can be added back — but then the server has to resequence on collision.

items.element: Assign person to a seat (TASK-342309) — assign-*.html + SeatingPlannerAssign.js
items.current: Opened from an empty seat's Assign button. Grouped by SOURCE, not role: “Event attendees” are read LIVE from the Unassigned tray (so the popup and the tray cannot disagree, and seating removes the tray row), “CRM contacts” are mock people not on the guest list — seating one says out loud that they were added to the event. Anyone already seated is filtered out. A row commits on click; there is no Save footer, because with one the row click would only be a selection. Predictive search matches name AND company across both groups; with no match it offers the typed term straight into the guest fields. Seating updates the seat row, the card dot, count and fill pill, the plan chip and the tray count. Esc closes. DOM-only.
items.needs: Write the TableSeat occupant — an FK to Attendee/Contact, or a guest name/company pair when there is no record — plus the role and the seat index. Seating a CRM contact must ALSO create the event Attendee row, in the same transaction. Reject anyone who already holds a seat in this event rather than duplicating them; the prototype filters them out of the list, but the server is the only place that can enforce it. Attendees via GET /crm/events/<id>/attendees?unassigned=1, contacts via GET /crm/contacts?q=, both debounced.

items.element: The Role field in the Assign popup
items.current: The brief lists a Role dropdown; the reference shows role as a BADGE on each result row and has no dropdown. Both are honoured: a person already in the system carries the role from their record (visible on the row before you click it), and the dropdown belongs to the manual guest — the one case with no record to read a role from. It defaults to Guest and covers all six roles.
items.needs: Confirm role is a property of the person, not of the seating. If it must be OVERRIDABLE when seating an existing person (“Tom is an attendee but he is hosting this table”), one-click seating has to become select-then-confirm, and the role then needs storing on TableSeat rather than read from the Attendee. That is a spec decision. Raised by this build.

items.element: Who is in which seat — data-sp-occupants on the table card
items.current: BUG FOUND AND FIXED during this build: occupant names for every table except Table 1 were DERIVED at render time from the mock people pool by index, so any change to the seats renamed everyone below it — unseat the third of ten and the remaining seven came back as different people, and a person assigned by this task lost their identity as soon as you switched tables. The shell now stamps the occupants onto the card whenever the seats change, so the card is the record. Verified: seat 4 assigned, switch away and back, still the same person; unseating seat 3 leaves seats 4–10 untouched.
items.needs: Nothing server-side — this is a prototype-only workaround for having no model. It does show what the real thing must guarantee: seat identity is a persisted TableSeat row keyed to an Attendee, never a position in a list. Also fixed the mock seed, which had the seven tray people ALSO in the seated pool, so the prototype claimed the same person was seated and unassigned at once.

items.element: What "unassigned" is measured against — plan or event
items.current: Implemented EVENT-WIDE: the pool excludes anyone seated in ANY plan of the event. The brief says "not yet seated in the selected plan", which taken literally would offer the 240 people seated in Main Ballroom as unassigned the moment you switch to Overflow Room B, and let you seat them a second time.
items.needs: Confirm the intended scope. Three things point to event-wide: the capacities say the plans are COMPLEMENTARY rather than alternatives (300 + 60 = 360 seats for 386 attendees, so both rooms seat one guest list); TASK-342309's Assign popup already excludes anyone seated anywhere, so per-plan here would make the two contradict each other; and event-wide is the reading that cannot double-book. If plans are meant to be ALTERNATIVE drafts of the same room, per-plan is right and the exclusion in 342309 has to change with it. Raised by this build.

items.element: Empty state of the Unassigned pool
items.current: Neither the brief nor the reference covers a pool with nobody in it — "0" over an empty box reads as broken. Added: a success-toned "Everyone is seated · Nobody is waiting for a seat" block, and a separate "nobody matches <term>" message for a filtered-out pool, which is a different situation from an empty one.
items.needs: Nothing server-side. Confirm the copy. Note the DS has no --ai-icon-success token (success exists only as surface/text/border), so the icon uses --ai-text-success, following the pattern .sp-capacity__note--warn already set — worth adding icon-status tokens if this recurs.

items.element: Who is seated where — data-sp-occupants on every card
items.current: Extends the 342309 fix. Occupant names used to be derived at RENDER time for any table but Table 1, so they only existed while a table was open — which a derived pool cannot work with, since it can only return a person it can name. Every card is now stamped at boot. Two defects fell out of that and were fixed: the mock generator put the SAME person in a dozen chairs (24 names over 300 seats), which meant unseating someone left them seated elsewhere and they never returned to the pool; and it could mint a name that was already authored or already in the pool. Names are now unique event-wide — verified 286 seated, 0 duplicates, 0 overlap with the pool.
items.needs: Nothing server-side — prototype scaffolding for having no model. It is the shape of the real requirement though: a seat holds a REFERENCE to an attendee, and every occupant of the event is a distinct person. Cosmetic artifact of guaranteeing uniqueness: people at the same table often share a surname. Real attendee data will not.

items.element: Placing a person without drag — the touch and keyboard path
items.current: The brief asks how this works on mobile. It is not a separate mobile feature: pick-then-place is the mechanism and drag is an accelerator for it. Tap (or Enter) a person in the pool or a seated row to pick them up — a fixed bar names them and offers Cancel — then tap a seat, a table card or the pool to place them. Esc or Cancel aborts. Rows carry tabindex, so the whole flow works from the keyboard, which matters because keyboard users cannot drag either. Verified in a browser: pick, place, swap, unseat, cancel and refusal all work by tap and by Enter, and picking does not hijack table selection.
items.needs: No extra backend — the same TableSeat writes. What is still OUTSTANDING is the mobile LAYOUT: the workspace has never been designed below --ai-bp-md, and this task did not invent it. The proposal from 344753 stands (plan chips as a scroll strip, single-column tables, seat panel and pool as sheets); pick-then-place is what makes it usable once that layout is built. Agreed with Mark: "we will refine mobile as we go".

items.element: Room layout (TASK-344760) — layout-*.html + SeatingPlannerLayout.js
items.current: Popup from the toolbar, titled with the plan name as the reference shows. Attaches a floor plan (PDF or image) to the PLAN, so switching plans switches the layout. The dropzone is the DS DragDropFile component; choose or drag a file and an IMAGE genuinely previews — it is read with FileReader, so nothing leaves the browser. A PDF gets a document card with an Open link rather than a fake thumbnail. Footer swaps Upload for Replace + Remove once something is attached. Non-image, non-PDF files are refused by name. The toolbar button carries a dot when the current plan has a layout — an addition, since otherwise you cannot tell without opening the popup.
items.needs: Upload to a MediaFileItem and store the REFERENCE on the SeatingPlan — one per plan. Replacing means repointing the reference and letting the media layer collect the old item, not deleting the file blind: a MediaFileItem may be shared. Validate type AND size server-side; the accept attribute is a convenience, not a control. Copying plans to another event (344756) needs a decision: does the clone carry the floor plan reference or start empty?

items.element: What "Room layout" means
items.current: RESOLVED. TASK-344753 assumed this was a spatial seat-map editor — dragging tables around a floor plan — and recorded it as undesigned. The brief settles it: Room layout ATTACHES A FILE. The tables grid stays a list, and no floor-plan canvas is needed.
items.needs: Nothing, unless a spatial view is wanted later — in which case it is a new task, not this one. Worth noting the attached plan is a picture: the app cannot relate a table on the canvas to a Table row, so "where table 12 actually is" stays human knowledge.

items.element: In-app preview of an attached PDF
items.current: The brief asks for in-app preview. Images do preview inline. A PDF cannot be rasterised by the page, so it shows a document card (name, size, Open in a new tab) plus a line saying why — better than a fake thumbnail that implies a preview that is not there.
items.needs: Decide whether inline PDF preview is required. If so it needs a viewer (pdf.js or an <embed>/<iframe> against the stored file), which is a real dependency and a decision for the spec team rather than something to slip in. Raised by this build.

items.element: Export the plan (TASK-342305) — export-*.html + SeatingPlannerExport.js
items.current: Split button in the toolbar — PDF (default) / Excel (.xlsx) / CSV — each opening a preview before download. THE PREVIEW FOLLOWS THE FORMAT: PDF previews as the document the reference draws (event name, meta line, then each table as a numbered list of occupants with the role in brackets), while CSV and .xlsx preview as the brief's six columns (Table, Type, Seat, Name, Company, Role) in the DS Table component — showing a document preview for a CSV would misrepresent the file. Read-only, per plan, derived from the DOM, and it stays true after edits: unseat someone and the row count and meta line both drop by one. THE CSV DOWNLOADS FOR REAL, generated in the browser with correct quoting; PDF and .xlsx explain that they are server-side rather than downloading something fake.
items.needs: Read-only over the plan's Table / TableSeat rows. PDF and XLSX need a server-side generator; build ALL THREE formats from the same query or the three will disagree — the browser CSV here only covers what the page already has. Note the row set is SEATED SEATS ONLY, per the brief ("every table and its seated attendees"); see seating-export-empty-seats.

items.element: Whether the export lists empty seats
items.current: It does not. The brief says "every table and its seated attendees", so a table with 3 of 10 filled exports 3 rows, and the preview says so out loud ("Empty seats are not exported"). A table with nobody seated still appears in the PDF, with a line saying it is empty, so it is not silently missing.
items.needs: Confirm. A planner printing a seating list may well want the empty seats as blank rows — it is the difference between a record of who is coming and a working document to fill in on the day. Cheap either way, but it changes the row count. Raised by this build.

items.element: Task number on the export controls
items.current: The shell marked these controls TASK-344761, taken from the parent task's sub-task list. The brief for the work is TASK-342305, so the controls now carry 342305.
items.needs: Confirm whether 344761 was simply a mis-recorded number, or a SEPARATE piece of export work that is still outstanding. Raised by this build.

items.element: Main interface (TASK-344753) — src/prototypes/SeatingPlanner/workspace.html
items.current: DECIDED 31 Jul 2026: the WORKLIST layout is the main interface. The two other alternatives, the compare board, the layout switcher, its demo bar and the four old fallback workspace states have been deleted; workspace.html is the only workspace file. Shape: tables list | table detail | unassigned, each region owning its own scroller so the PAGE never scrolls and both ends of a drag stay on screen — the defect this replaced put the pool's first row at y~1013 in a page-scrolled 1356px document, so you could see the seats or the pool but never both. Detail column minmax(320, 384) and pool 320, both draggable wider from those minimums, never narrower; the tables list flips between rows and 240px cards (grid by default); below 1024 the pool is hidden, the toggle goes, and the table detail opens inline beneath the tapped row. ALL 13 SUB-TASKS ARE WIRED HERE — verified by clicking every [data-sp-action] at 1440 and 500 and asserting the shell's 'not built in this task' toast never appears, plus plan switch, table select, seat reorder, unseat, drag, filters, both searches and the export split menu. Two things had never been wired in ANY layout and were fixed to get there: Table types (342308) had a handler but no trigger anywhere, and Change event (342608) had no handler at all.
items.needs: Nothing server-side for the layout itself. Build it from workspace.html rather than from the old frames. Note the shell CSS/JS is still .sp-shell-scoped and additive, because SeatingPlanner.css also paints screen 1 and the 34 sub-task capture states — those states still carry the old .sp-ws__cols markup, which is why DeletePlan.js keeps that selector alongside the [data-sp-workspace] hook. Open items elsewhere in this surface: seating-card-keyboard (cards bind click only — Enter cannot open a table), seating-workspace-prefs (pane widths and the tables view do not persist), and seating-card-left-border (fixed in the shell scope only).

items.element: Pane widths and tables-view preference — SeatingPlannerShellAlts.js
items.current: Both are in-memory only and last as long as the page does. Dragging a resize handle writes a px width to a CSS custom property on the pane row; the list/grid toggle writes one attribute on <body>. Reload and both return to their defaults (grid view, detail 384 easing to 320, pool 320).
items.needs: Persist per user, not per event or per plan — it is a workspace preference, like a column layout in a data grid: {tablesView: 'list'|'grid', detailWidth: px|null, poolWidth: px|null}, null meaning 'use the default and keep adapting to the viewport'. Store the widths as numbers and clamp them server-side or on read, because a stale width from a wide monitor must not squeeze the tables list below its floor on a laptop — the front end already clamps to the same floor it uses in CSS. Cheap to defer: without it the layout simply opens at its defaults every time.

items.element: Worklist v1 below 1024px — SeatingPlannerShell.css @media (max-width: 1023px) + SeatingPlannerShellAlts.js
items.current: Built and working. HTML5 drag does not fire on touch at all, so the Unassigned column — whose whole job was to be dragged out of — is hidden and seating happens by tapping an empty seat and picking from the Assign popup, which reads the same derived list (already the canonical path on every viewport, TASK-344759). HIDDEN, NOT REMOVED: [data-sp-tray-list] is a singleton nine queries depend on and the derived pool is where unseated people go, so unseat / delete table / delete plan all still work; its count is mirrored into the tables pane head ('7 unassigned') so the 'somebody is still waiting' signal survives. The table detail opens INLINE beneath the row you tapped, spanning the full viewport width, using the same relocation machinery as layout C gated by body[data-sp-acc-below] — inline rather than absolutely positioned so DOM order stays reading order for a screen reader and the Tab key, and nothing needs re-measuring on scroll. Nothing is open on arrival; tapping a row scrolls it to the top of the page smoothly (instant under prefers-reduced-motion); tapping the open row again closes it, and the close is ANIMATED — the drawer's height eases to zero so the rows below slide up instead of jumping 800px, with a token guard so tapping another table mid-animation cannot leave a collapsed drawer behind. The seating plans strip stays on screen (switching rooms is a mobile job too): the chips and the layout switcher scroll sideways in one line rather than wrapping, which is what had made the appbar 480px tall. The list/grid toggle is HIDDEN below 1024: both the row restyle and the grid-view rules live inside min-width blocks, so down there the cards render as the shipped card one per row whichever way the toggle is set — measured one per row at 500, 768 and 1023 — and a control that changes nothing is worse than no control. The body attribute is left in place so widening the window returns you to the view you were in.
items.needs: Nothing server-side. Two open design questions: (1) there is no way to browse the unassigned people on their own below 1024 — only via Assign from an empty seat — so a tappable 'N unassigned' opening a bottom sheet would close that gap, and the count is currently plain text; (2) the seat rows keep their draggable attributes on mobile, harmless because touch never fires them, but they could be stripped. Note two behaviours inherited from the shell, both reasonable but worth knowing: Add table opens the table it just created, and switching plans opens the new plan's first table. Transitions and smooth scrolling do not run under headless virtual time, so both were verified by destination and by timeout fallback rather than by observing the animation — worth an eyeball in a real browser below 1024.

items.element: Keyboard operation of a table card — SeatingPlannerWorkspace.js initTableSelect
items.current: DEFECT, pre-existing and present on every layout including the current one. The cards are role="button" tabindex="0", so they take focus and announce as buttons, but initTableSelect binds CLICK only and the shell has no keydown handler for them (its single keydown listener handles Escape for the export split menu). A div with role=button does not synthesise a click from Enter, so a keyboard user can focus a table and not open it. Space scrolls the page instead.
items.needs: Add a keydown handler beside initTableSelect: on Enter or Space with a [data-sp-table] target, preventDefault and call selectTable(card). One place, all layouts fixed at once — the mobile accordion's close-on-second-tap would then need the same treatment. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, and it also blocks the mobile detail from being opened without a pointer. Found while building the mobile layout; deliberately NOT fixed there, because it is the shell's own gap and shell edits have been kept to the single line this exploration needed.

items.element: Left edge of an untiered (Standard) table card — .sp-table
items.current: DEFECT, fixed in the alternatives only. A Standard table carries no data-sp-tier attribute, so it never reaches `.sp-table[data-sp-tier] { border-left-color: var(--sp-tier-colour, transparent) }` and keeps the base `border-left: 3px solid transparent` — measured rgba(0,0,0,0) against a 1px #e2e2e3 frame on every other side, i.e. a card with one edge missing. The alternatives now give an untiered card the frame colour, excluding the selected card so its brand edge still wins: every row has a 3px left edge, neutral when untiered and coloured when tiered, and the text stays aligned across rows (a 1px left border would shift it 2px against tiered rows).
items.needs: Move the one-liner into SeatingPlanner.css when a layout is adopted — `.sp-table:not([data-sp-tier]):not(.sp-table--selected) { border-left-color: var(--ai-border-secondary) }`. It is kept out of that file for now because it paints the 35 signed-off states and the current layout is deliberately untouched, so THE FALLBACK STILL SHOWS THE GAP. Related pre-existing subtlety worth a designer's eye: on a tiered card the tier colour outranks the selected state on that edge, so an open Gold table shows a gold left edge and brand on its other three sides.

items.element: Seating plans block — .sp-plans in the layout alternatives
items.current: Rebuilt as two rows: the title with New plan and Copy plans to event on one line, the rooms beneath on their own horizontally scrollable line. Desktop gets prev/next ARROWS instead of a scrollbar — hidden until the rooms overflow, and each hides again at its end, so a visible arrow always does something. Touch gets a swipe with no arrow. The room cards KEEP their size-4 (240px) width below 1024 rather than stretching to fill the track, so the cut card at the edge is emergent rather than guaranteed: measured with five plans, a card is cut at 500, 560, 600, 700, 768 and 900px (10% to 97% of a card showing), but at ~527, ~775 and 1023px the cards land exactly flush (track = 248n - 8) and nothing would signal the rest. So a TRAILING FADE is applied whenever the track can still scroll right — a mask driven by the same measurement that hides the next arrow — which does not depend on the arithmetic working out. The data-sp-plans-row hook moved onto the track, so NewPlan.js's chips and DeletePlan.js's 'No plans yet' hint still land in the right place with no change to either module.
items.needs: Nothing server-side. Three implementation notes: the arrow and fade state is re-synced on scroll, on resize, on a mutation of the chip list AND on a timeout after an arrow click, because a smooth scroll fires no scroll events in some environments and a stale arrow is a dead control; the fade uses currentColor as its opaque mask stop, because a mask reads only the alpha channel and hardcoding a colour would breach the token rule; and if the fade is ever dropped, remember the peek is NOT guaranteed at 527, 775 or 1023px with 240px cards.

items.element: What is left in src/prototypes/SeatingPlanner/ after the 31 Jul cleanup
items.current: 40 HTML files: workspace.html (the adopted main interface), 4 screen-1 event-picker states (index, all-events, search-active, no-results), 34 sub-task capture states, states.html (the index, not a screen) and _base-workspace.html (a BUILD INPUT, not a screen — the generator reads it to rebuild workspace.html with all ten modal roots intact; it is not linked from anywhere). Deleted: alt1-threepane.html, alt1b-worklist-v2.html, alt3-accordion.html, alt-compare.html and workspace-{no-event,no-plan,plan-selected,free-seats}.html.
items.needs: Nothing. Recorded because the prototype directory is UNTRACKED — those eight files have no git history and cannot be recovered, so this is the only record that they existed and what replaced them. The Figma frames captured from them still exist on page 2025:803 and are the designer's reference; the superseded ones want deleting by hand.

items.element: Room Card (`src/components/RoomCard/`) — the DS component built 2026-08-25 from Figma `3470:84951`
items.current: Room name, table count, seated count and capacity are hardcoded in the demo. The capacity bar is driven by a `--room-card-progress` custom property the caller sets; the component computes nothing. Selection is a class the parent toggles — the card ships no JS, so nothing coordinates single-select yet. Edit and delete are unwired.
items.needs: **RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — a Room Card IS a room/plan card**, the componentised form of the plan chip in `seating-plan-chip-summary`. Not a new entity above `SeatingPlan`, so **no new table is needed**: name is the plan name, and `tableCount` / `seatsSeated` / `seatsCapacity` all derive from the plan's `Table` + `TableSeat` rows. Serve as `GET /crm/events/{eventId}/plans` → `[{ id, name, tableCount, seatsSeated, seatsCapacity }]`, with the caller computing `seatsSeated/seatsCapacity` into `--room-card-progress`. **Derive the counts server-side, not on the client** — the exact trap already recorded in `seating-plan-chip-summary`, where a written-once summary silently went stale after an unseat. Any sub-task that changes table or seat counts must re-read them rather than patching the card. Delete needs a confirmation plus a decision on what happens to the tables and seated attendees underneath (cf. `seating-delete-plan`). **Front-end follow-up:** the prototype still renders its own hand-built plan chip — replace it with this component so the two cannot drift.

items.element: Table Card (`src/components/TableCard/`) — the DS component built 2026-08-25 from Figma `3470:85483`
items.current: Table name, tier, sponsor, per-role seat counts and capacity are all hardcoded in the demo. The capacity bar is proportional but the component computes nothing — each segment's seat count arrives as a `--seg` custom property the caller sets. Selection is a class the parent toggles; edit and delete are unwired buttons.
items.needs: `GET /crm/plans/{planId}/tables` -> `[{ id, name, tableType, sponsor, capacity, seats: [{ role }] }]`. **Aggregate the per-role counts server-side** and hand them straight to `--seg` — the same trap as `seating-plan-chip-summary`, where a client-computed summary went stale after an unseat and silently lied. The role set must match the `--sp-*` collection; note Figma's legend omits Host even though the collection and AttendeeCard both define it, so confirm whether a table can seat a host before the contract is fixed. Tier comes from `seating-table-types`; sponsor from `seating-table-form`. Edit opens `seating-edit-table`, delete `seating-delete-table` — both already specced. The bar is decorative for assistive tech (`aria-hidden`), so the legend text is the accessible representation and must carry real counts.

items.element: Table Detail (`src/patterns/TableDetail/`) — the DS pattern built 2026-08-25 from Figma `3475:94010`
items.current: Table name, tier, sponsor, seated count and every seat row are hardcoded. The role legend is hand-written in the demo. The panel fills its column and the seat list scrolls, but nothing is wired: delete, reorder and Assign are AttendeeCard's unwired buttons, and the seat rows are drop targets whose class the parent would toggle.
items.needs: `GET /crm/tables/{tableId}` → `{ id, name, tableType, sponsor, capacity, seats: [{ index, attendee, role }] }`. **The legend is DERIVED from the distinct roles actually seated — do not store it**, which is why Type=Default has no legend rather than an empty one. Derive the seated count server-side too, the same trap as `seating-plan-chip-summary`. Assign routes to `seating-assign-seat`, delete/reorder to `seating-seat-occupant-record`; the drop target is `seating-drag-assign`. Roles must match the `--sp-*` collection — this legend covers all five including Host, unlike TableCard's which omits it. **Mobile note:** the pattern hides its header below 768px on the assumption that the mobile sheet supplies the table name and count; if that chrome changes, the header decision needs revisiting because a screen-reader user would otherwise get an unnamed list of seats.

items.element: Table Listing (`src/patterns/TableListing/`) — the DS pattern built 2026-08-25 from Figma `3488:196339`: the tables grid plus its toolbar
items.current: The table list, the counts, the search and the "Only free seats" toggle are all hardcoded. The toggle is a real `role="switch"` and the search a real `type="search"`, but neither is wired — the pattern renders what it is given. The grid is responsive on its own (auto-fill), so column count needs nothing from the backend.
items.needs: Per-table data reuses **`seating-tables-grid`** — this item covers only the toolbar. **"Only free seats"** filters to tables with capacity remaining: derive it server-side from the same aggregated per-role counts rather than filtering a client list, and see **`seating-free-seats-filter`** which already specs the behaviour. The **search** filters by table name; debounce a `?q=` against the same tables endpoint rather than filtering in the browser, so a plan with 200 tables behaves. **Open question:** a `View Actions` frame (two 32×32 buttons, presumably grid/list view) sits hidden at the end of the toolbar in Figma and was not built — confirm whether it is coming, since it changes the toolbar's right-hand group and may need a persisted view preference (cf. `seating-workspace-prefs`).

items.element: Seating Header (`src/patterns/SeatingHeader/`) — the DS pattern built 2026-08-26 from Figma `3474:90519`: the event info bar, the room selector and the tables toolbar
items.current: Every value is hardcoded: the event name, date, attendee count and venue; the plan list; the active room's name and its unassigned count. The "Show unassigned" switch flips itself (Toggle.js) and reports `toggle:change`, but nothing listens. Copy Plans, New Plan, the event-switch button, Room Layout, Add Table, Export and the kebab are all unwired. Type=No Plans is markup the caller chooses, not a state the pattern derives.
items.needs: **Event header:** `GET /crm/events/{eventId}` → `{ name, date, attendeeCount, venue }` for the info bar. The **event-switch** button implies a picker over the same list `seating-events-list` already specs. **Plan list** reuses **`seating-room-list`** — this item adds only the strip around it, and whether it scrolls is a front-end concern already handled. **Which plan is selected** is the workspace-level selection `seating-workspace-prefs` covers. **The unassigned count** for the active room is the same aggregate **`seating-tables-listing`** needs; derive it server-side, never store it — exactly the trap `seating-plan-chip-summary` documents, where a written-once summary went stale after an unseat and silently lied. **"Show unassigned"** toggles the unassigned tray's visibility, so it is a view preference rather than a query (cf. `seating-workspace-prefs`); it is NOT the same thing as `seating-free-seats-filter`. **Copy Plans / New Plan** reuse `seating-copy-plans` and `seating-new-plan`; **Add Table** reuses `seating-add-table`; **Export** reuses `seating-export`; **Room Layout** reuses `seating-room-layout`. **Has Plans vs No Plans** should follow from the plan list being empty — the empty case is the `No Plans` variant, which is the bar alone. **Open:** the kebab menu's contents are undefined — Figma draws the trigger only, so someone needs to say what is in it.

items.element: Seating Toast (`src/components/SeatingToast/`) — the DS component built 2026-08-26 from Figma `3474:90240`: the action confirmation / warning pill with an Undo
items.current: The messages, the emphasised names and the Undo button are all hardcoded. The pill is presentational: it owns no show/hide, no auto-dismiss timer and no JS at all — unlike the `Toast` card, it has no close button to wire. `role="status"` (Success) and `role="alert"` (Error) are in place, so a screen reader announces it once it is inserted.
items.needs: **Undo is the whole point of this component and it is the part that needs the backend.** A toast is raised by a seating action — see `seating-assign-seat`, `seating-drag-assign`, `seating-touch-placement` — and its Undo must reverse *that specific* operation, so each action needs to return an operation/undo id that the toast carries and posts back. A blanket "undo last change" is the wrong contract: two toasts can be on screen at once, and the user may undo the older one. **Failure messages** ("Table 12 is full") should come from the server's rejection of the assign, not be composed client-side, so the reason stays truthful when the rule changes — cf. `seating-capacity-reduction`. **Who retires a toast** is a front-end decision that has not been made: the component deliberately has no timer, so the app shell needs an auto-dismiss policy (and Undo must not vanish before it can be clicked — WCAG 2.2.1 wants a way to extend or dismiss). **Open:** `Show Cta = false` is a real Figma boolean that neither drawn variant exercises, so the CTA-less pill's 46px height is emergent rather than specified; confirm whether a toast should change height depending on whether it offers an Undo.

items.element: Seating Planner screen (`src/cc/templates/SeatingPlanner/`) — the Tier=Template screen built 2026-08-26 from Figma `3515:175956` (desktop) / `3515:213358` (mobile), inside the CC app shell. Screens 1-3 of a series: "No Event", the "Select Event" modal, and "No Plan" (event chosen, no plans yet)
items.current: The screen renders the empty state unconditionally — there is no event, plan or seating data behind it, and "Select Event" is inert. The CC shell around it (rail, chrome, breadcrumb, right ActionsMenu, AiAssistant) is ported from ControlScreen and carries that screen's own hardcoded content: the breadcrumb reads Affino.com > Events > Seating Planner as static text, and the user block still says Derrick Jefferson. The Select Event button now opens the EventPicker modal for real (open/close/backdrop/Escape/focus all wired), but the event list inside it is the picker's own hardcoded rows, and choosing one only closes the modal and re-emits `seating-planner:event-chosen` — nothing consumes it yet. Choosing an event now advances the screen to the "No Plan" state for real, which renders SeatingHeader (Type=No Plans) over a dashed placeholder card; `?state=no-plan` lands there directly. The header's event name, date, venue and its Copy Plans / New Plan buttons are all still hardcoded and unwired.
items.needs: **Which state this screen renders is the event gate** — see `seating-event-gate`. With no event chosen it shows this empty state and nothing else; once one is chosen the same `.seating-screen` card holds the planner (`seating-header`, `seating-tables-listing`, `seating-table-detail`, `seating-unassigned-tray`). **"Select Event"** opens the picker that `seating-events-list` specs, and the chosen event should persist per user so a reload returns to it — `seating-last-used-event` already covers that. **The breadcrumb needs to be real**: the trailing crumb is the screen, but "Events" and the zone selector are navigation the shell should supply, not this template. **The shell's user block is ControlScreen's placeholder** and needs the authenticated user, which is a CC-shell concern rather than a seating one. **Open (design, not backend):** Figma shows no page header beyond the breadcrumb, so the screen has no title element; and the mobile chrome question — Figma draws the top nav at 48 where the TopNavigation component's own rule gives 40 — needs a designer ruling, since it affects every CC screen and not just this one. **The picker's own data and persistence are already specced on it** — `GET /crm/events?status=live&q=&sort=-startDate` and the per-user last-used event — see `seating-events-list` and `seating-last-used-event`; this screen only needs to consume the selection. **`seating-planner:event-chosen` is the seam**: its `{ id, name }` should load the planner into the same `.seating-screen` card and persist the choice. **Open (design):** there is no scrim token in the scale (both themes are raw rgba), and the dark-mode scrim density is likely system-wide rather than specific to this screen. **Which state renders is the plan COUNT, not the click** — an event that already has plans must go straight to the planner, not to No Plan, so the front end needs the plan list (or at least its length) with the event; see `seating-room-list`. **New Plan** in the header is what leaves this state — see `seating-new-plan` for what it must create (a plan generates its tables, per the empty state's own copy). **The SeatingHeader's event details** should come from the chosen event rather than its hardcoded copy, which is the same data `seating-header` already specs.
